newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks surge to end at record close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks surge to end at record close.

text.p: SPI futures 2394 +30 US 30yr cl 6.83 -0.03
*Shares surged to a new record high close after wages data
supported rate cut hopes. Volume 387.0 million shares, value A$793.3
million, 1,086 stocks traded, 313 steady, 465 rises, 308 falls

Australian shares finished at a record closing high on Thursday after the market opened higher in defiance of a weaker Dow and garnered strength from wages data which heightened speculation of an interest rates cut soon.
The All Ordinaries index closed up 30.9 points at 2,377.6, 11.4 points above last week's previous record close of 2366.2.
The December share price index finished up 30 points at 2,394 and at a 16.4 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said the wage figures confirmed the market's bullish opening stance and follow-through buying was evident for bank stocks and other cyclical sectors after the data was released.
"The wages data spurred the market, it was the crucial factor that pushed up yielding stocks," said a dealer from Brisbane broker, Burrell & Co.
Investors would be encouraged by the Australian market's rare show of independence from Wall Street, the dealer said.
"It indicates a belief that the Australian market is still undervalued compared to the U.S. market," he said.

Dealers said that although rate-sensitive issues such as banks, transport and media stocks made the best gains on the day, the rise was underpinned by steady buying interest in key resource stocks BHP, CRA and WMC.
Amongst the big miners, WMC continued to be a favoured stock with dealers saying the company's shares had been oversold in the previous month on concerns about falling base metal prices.
News Corp was an outstanding performer on the day, its stock continuing a recovery started in New York after being sold down earlier in the week on a broker's sell recommendation.

Colly Cotton, one of Australia's largest cotton production and ginning companies, made an impressive debut. The stock opened at an 11 percent premium to its issue price of A$1.00 and closed at A$1.12 after touching an intra-day high of A$1.14.

In other markets, bond yields slipped to the lowest levels since March 1994 after August quarter wages rose just 0.7 percent. The yield on 10-year T-bonds finished at 7.39 percent, down 0.15 percent from Wednesday's closing levels.
The Australian dollar fell 1/4 cent after weak wages data adding further weight to calls for a rate cut. At 5.15 p.m. (0515 GMT) the unit was quoted at US$0.7923/28.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives trade was extremely active with option business dominated by trade in BHP calls.
